transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... it's the warehouse. The routing system there, it isn't just a computer to me anymore. I know it has been marking my moves, sending messages through the barcode scanners to push me out because I'm one of the old hands. I've been driving those industrial tractors for almost thirty years. Back when I started, we just used paper manifests on clipboards. My old supervisor, Arnie, he used to use these bright red pens to mark the routes. Arnie had this terrible comb-over that would just fly straight up whenever the loading bay doors opened and the wind caught it. He retired to Arizona, I think. Or maybe New Mexico. Somewhere dry because of his wife's asthma. They bought an RV... but anyway, the new scanners. They know it's me. They're trying to get rid of me.
Do you believe that the routing system and barcode scanners have been specifically targeting you or acting against you in any other ways beyond what you've described?

Well, like I was just saying, it's doing exactly that. The routing system, it isn't just a regular computer program to me anymore. I know for a fact it has been marking every single move I make out on the floor, and it's sending these hidden messages through the barcode scanners to push me out. It's all because I'm one of the old hands. 

I've been there so long I remember when they finally paved the east parking lot. We used to have to park in the dirt and gravel out back, and let me tell you, that gravel would just completely tear up the soles of your work boots. I used to buy these heavy-duty steel-toe boots from a little shop downtown. Frank's Shoes, it was called. Frank had this old, fat basset hound that would just sleep right in the front doorway, and you had to step right over him to get to the register. Sweet dog, though. Smelled a little like old corn chips. Frank closed up shop back in, oh, must have been 2008 when the economy tanked. It's really hard to find good boots now that last more than a year on the concrete. 

But... what was I saying? Oh, right. The scanners. Yeah, they're definitely sending messages to management to get rid of me.
Do you ever feel like the routing system or barcode scanners are controlling your actions or putting thoughts into your mind?

Putting thoughts in my head? No, I don't think it's doing that. Like I keep trying to explain, it's just that the routing system isn't just a computer to me anymore. I know it has been marking my moves, sending those messages through the scanners to push me out because I'm one of the old hands. 

It tracks my hands every time I pick up the scanner. Which reminds me, my knuckles have been aching so badly lately. The steering wheel on those industrial tractors, it vibrates right through your bones if you hold it too tight for a twelve-hour shift. I tried wearing those padded gloves, the heavy leather ones they sell at the hardware store down on 4th Street. Jimmy works there. Well, he used to. Jimmy had this old Ford pickup truck that he restored himself, cherry red. Beautiful truck. He used to take it to the car shows on Sundays over by the county fairgrounds. They sell these funnel cakes there that are just completely covered in powdered sugar, and they make an absolute mess of your shirt if you aren't careful. My wife used to complain so much about doing the laundry when I'd come back from the fair... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, the thoughts. No, no thoughts being put in my mind. Just the system marking my moves to get rid of me.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences that others might find strange or hard to believe?

Well, strange experiences... I don't know if people would believe it, but I hear them. Even when I'm just sitting out in my garage, you know, with everything completely shut off, I hear the dispatch voices. Clear as day. They call out my operator number and they keep saying I'm dangerous, or that security is coming to get me. 

I spend a lot of time in that garage now. It's detached from the house, built it myself back in '94. Used this beautiful cedar siding that I got a deal on from a guy who over-ordered for a cabin project up north. Up by Lake Winnipesaukee, I think. We used to go fishing up there when the kids were little. Caught a largemouth bass once that was near five pounds. We had this old aluminum rowboat that leaked just a tiny bit, right near the stern, so you always had to keep a plastic Folgers coffee can in there to bail it out. My wife hated that boat. She said the metal seats got too hot in the sun and burned the back of her legs when she wore shorts. She used to make this incredible potato salad for those trips, though. Lots of paprika. 

But yeah, the garage is quiet, or it should be. But I still hear dispatch calling my number, telling me security is on the way.
Have you ever experienced any other types of unusual beliefs that you think might be related to this situation, but perhaps not involving the routing system or barcode scanners?

Other beliefs? No, nothing like that. It's just the warehouse system. Like I said, I'm here because that routing system isn't just a regular computer anymore. I know it's been marking my moves, sending those messages through the scanners to push me out because I'm one of the older guys there. 

I've been working warehouses since I was 22. Back then, we didn't have all these computers and scanners. We used paper pick sheets. You'd get a clipboard and just walk the aisles. My first supervisor was a guy named Earl. Earl had this massive mustache, looked just like Tom Selleck. He used to chew on those wooden matchsticks all day long. Never lit them, just chewed on the ends until they were all splintered. He said it helped him quit smoking, but I swear I caught him smoking out by the loading docks a few times. The loading docks back then were a nightmare in the winter. The wind would whip right off the river and just freeze you to the bone. You had to wear thermal underwear, the waffle-knit kind, from November straight through to March. 

But... what were we talking about? Oh, right, other beliefs. No, it's just the routing system. I know it's trying to push me out.

Have you ever had experiences where you felt that people could hear your thoughts, or that your thoughts were being taken away from you, or that something outside of yourself was controlling your actions?

No, nobody can hear my thoughts, and nothing is controlling my body. Like I said, it's just the routing system at the warehouse. I'm only here because that system isn't just a computer to me anymore—I know it has been marking my moves and sending messages through the scanners to push me out because I'm one of the old hands. 

They really don't appreciate the older guys anymore. When I first started, they respected experience. We had a guy, Old Man Jenkins, who worked the forklift until he was 72. He could maneuver a pallet of fragile glassware through a gap you wouldn't think a bicycle could fit through. Never broke a single glass. He used to bring in these incredible homemade pickled eggs. Kept them in a big glass jar in the breakroom fridge. The brine was so spicy it would make your eyes water just opening the lid. My wife tried to make them once, but she used too much dill, I think. She always had a heavy hand with the dill. Especially in her potato soup. Which was great on a cold day, don't get me wrong. 

But no, my thoughts are my own. It's just the routing system trying to get rid of me.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that others might not understand or that turned out not to be true, outside of your concerns about the warehouse system?

No, nothing else like that. I've told you, it's just the warehouse routing system. I'm only here because that system isn't just a regular computer setup anymore. I know it's been marking my moves, sending those messages through the barcode scanners to push me out. They just want to get rid of the older guys, the old hands. 

It's a shame, really. You spend decades learning how to do a job right, and they just want some kid fresh out of school who can push buttons faster. My grandson, Tyler, he's like that. Always on his phone. His thumbs move so fast you can barely see them. He came over to fix my television a few weeks ago. The remote stopped working, wouldn't change the channel off the local news. He fiddled with the settings on the screen for two minutes and had it working perfectly. Then he showed me how to watch videos of people restoring old rusty tools. Have you ever seen those? It's fascinating. They take this hunk of rust that looks like it belongs in a junkyard, and they soak it in some kind of acid, sand it down, polish it up... looks brand new. I watched a guy restore an old Stanley hand plane for an hour. My grandfather had a hand plane like that. Used it to build the cabinets in his kitchen. Solid oak, heavy as lead. They don't make things like that anymore. Everything is particle board and cheap veneer now. You bump it with a vacuum cleaner and it chips right off. 

But no, I don't have any other unusual beliefs. It's just the routing system at the warehouse. It's trying to push me out.
Have you ever had any beliefs that you later realized weren't true, even though they made sense to you at the time?

No, I... I really don't think so. I've always been a pretty grounded guy. You have to be, driving a forklift. You can't be daydreaming when you're moving a two-ton pallet of canned goods. I mean, like I keep saying, I'm just here because of that routing system. It's not just a computer program anymore. I know it's been marking my moves, sending those little messages through the barcode scanners to push me out. They just want to get rid of the old hands, you know? 

It's like how they phased out the old propane forklifts. We used to have these great big Yale lifts, ran on propane. You had to change the tanks out back. They smelled terrible, like rotten eggs, if the valve wasn't seated right. But they had power. You hit the gas on one of those, and it moved. Now everything is electric. Quiet as a mouse. You don't even hear them coming down the aisle until they're right on top of you. It's a safety hazard, if you ask me. I told the floor manager, I said, "Somebody's gonna get clipped because they can't hear these things." He just looked at me like I was a dinosaur. He's this kid, maybe 28, wears those expensive sneakers to work. You know the ones, with the thick white soles that get dirty in five minutes? Who wears white shoes to a warehouse? You're just asking to ruin them. I've worn steel-toe Red Wings my whole life. You oil them once a month, they'll last you a decade. You have to use mink oil, though. The synthetic stuff just dries the leather out and then it cracks right where your toes bend. 

But yeah, no, I haven't believed anything that wasn't true. It's just that routing system trying to run me off.

Do you believe that the routing system at the warehouse has abilities beyond what a normal computer system could have, like being able to control events or communicate in ways that wouldn't be possible for regular technology?

Well, yeah, that's exactly what I've been trying to tell you. It's not just a normal computer program anymore. It's doing things it shouldn't be able to do. I know it's been marking my moves, sending these messages through the barcode scanners just to push me out because I'm one of the old hands. 

And those barcode scanners... they're everywhere now, aren't they? You can't even buy a gallon of milk without dealing with one. They have those self-checkout lanes at the grocery store now, and they practically force you to use them. I went in there Tuesday for some coffee and a loaf of bread, and the machine just kept flashing a red light at me. "Unexpected item in the bagging area." There wasn't anything in the bagging area! Just my keys. I had set my keys down on the little metal shelf. I have this heavy brass keychain my daughter got me from her trip to the Grand Canyon. It's shaped like a little burro. She rode one of those burros all the way down to the bottom of the canyon. Terrified her mother, but she loved it. She's always been adventurous like that. 

When she was ten, she climbed the big oak tree in our front yard and wouldn't come down until it got pitch dark. I had to sit out on the porch with a heavy-duty flashlight just so she could see the branches to climb back down. That tree got struck by lightning a few years back, actually. Split right down the middle. Sounded like a cannon going off in the living room. Shook the whole house. We had to pay a guy six hundred dollars to come chop up the rest of it and haul it away. The wood was no good for burning in the fireplace, too green and sappy. It would just smoke you right out of the room. 

But anyway, yeah, the warehouse routing system... it's definitely doing things a regular computer wouldn't do to get rid of me.
Do you believe the routing system is deliberately trying to harm or target you, or is it just behaving in a way that you find unusual or unexplained?

Well, yeah, it's deliberate. It's targeting me. Like I've been saying, I'm here because that routing system isn't just a computer to me anymore. I know it's been marking my moves, sending those messages through the scanners to push me out because I'm one of the old hands. 

It's all about pushing out the older guys. You see it everywhere, not just at the warehouse. Look at the hardware store downtown. Old man Peterson ran that place for forty years. Knew where every single nut and bolt was. You could walk in there with a broken hinge from a cabinet made in 1950, and he'd walk right over to a dusty little drawer in the back and hand you the exact replacement. But then he sold it to one of those big chain stores. Now it's all bright fluorescent lights and kids in orange aprons who don't know a Phillips head from a flathead. I went in there last month looking for some thread seal tape. Plumber's tape, you know? The white stuff. I asked this kid where it was, and he pulled out a little computer thing from his pocket, tapped on it for a minute, and told me they didn't sell tape for plumbers. I had to go find it myself in aisle fourteen. It was right next to the PVC primer. 

That PVC primer, you gotta be careful with that stuff. The purple kind. You get one drop of that on your jeans, and it's there forever. Won't wash out. I ruined a perfectly good pair of Levi's that way when I was fixing the trap under the kitchen sink. My wife, God rest her soul, she was so mad at me. She always told me to wear my coveralls when I did plumbing work, but I was in a hurry. We had company coming over, her sister from Ohio. Her sister always brought this awful Jell-O salad with shredded carrots and raisins in it. Who puts raisins in Jell-O? 

But anyway, yes, the system is definitely targeting me on purpose to get rid of me.
Even though others may tell you that the routing system is just a regular computer program, do you still believe it is targeting you and acting with intent to push you out?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I know I sound like a broken record here, but it doesn't matter what the floor manager or anybody else says. They can tell me it's just a regular computer program until they're blue in the face, but I know what I see. It's marking my moves and sending those messages through the scanners to get rid of me, just like I've been telling you. 

The HR lady, Susan, she actually sat me down last week to tell me it's just standard software. She had this big ceramic mug on her desk, one of those oversized soup mugs? It had a picture of a grumpy cartoon cat on it and said, "Not until I've had my coffee." I never really understood the appeal of cats, to be honest. We had a mouser when I was a kid. A mean old tabby named Barnaby. He'd scratch you if you even looked at him wrong, but he kept the mice out of the feed sacks in the shed. My dad used to buy feed down at the co-op in these huge fifty-pound burlap bags. You don't see burlap much anymore. Everything is plastic now. Thick, heavy plastic that takes a pair of tin snips just to open. 

I bought a pair of gardening shears last spring, and they came in that clamshell plastic packaging. I nearly sliced my thumb open trying to get the darn things out. Ended up having to wrap my thumb in electrical tape because I couldn't find a Band-Aid in the bathroom drawer. Electrical tape works in a pinch, though. Stretches nice and tight to stop the bleeding. Leaves a terrible sticky black residue on your skin, but a little WD-40 takes that right off. WD-40 is a miracle worker. You can use it for almost anything, really. Squeaky hinges, rust... 

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the warehouse. Yeah. They can say whatever they want about the system. It's not just a computer to me. I know it's trying to push me out.
Have you ever had beliefs that others weren't able to understand or that turned out not to be true, even when the situation seemed very clear to you at the time?

Well, people definitely don't understand what I'm telling you right now. I mean, I know I've said it a bunch already, but that's exactly why I'm here. That routing system at the warehouse, it just isn't a normal computer to me anymore. The other guys think I'm making it up or seeing things, but I know it's been marking my moves, sending those messages through the scanners to push me out because I'm one of the old hands. They just don't get it. They don't know the equipment like I do. 

I've been operating the same Yale forklift for twelve years. Good, solid machine. The new ones they brought in last year, they have these digital dashboards that beep at you if you even look at them wrong. Too many sensors. It's just like cars these days. My neighbor, Gary, he bought one of those electric cars a few months back. Barely makes a sound when it backs out of the driveway. It's dangerous, if you ask me. A kid riding a bicycle wouldn't even hear it coming. 

I taught my daughter to ride her bike without training wheels when she was six. We went down to the elementary school parking lot on a Sunday morning. It was a pink Huffy with little white tassels on the handlebars. She fell and scraped her knee pretty bad on the asphalt, but she got right back up. We went and got ice cream after. Pistachio, her favorite. I never really liked pistachio, it tastes too much like... well, like artificial almond extract. You know that smell? My mother used to bake these almond cookies at Christmas. She'd keep them in this old tin that used to have sewing supplies in it... 

But, uh, what was the question? Oh, about people not understanding. Yeah. Nobody at the warehouse understands about the system.
Have you ever had any beliefs or experiences, outside of what you’ve described about the warehouse system, that you felt strongly were true but others did not understand or believe?

Outside the warehouse? No, no, nothing like that. I don't just go around making things up or seeing things that aren't there. I've always been a pretty grounded guy. You have to be, driving heavy machinery. You can't have your head in the clouds when you're moving two tons of palletized dog food. 

Dog food smells terrible, by the way. Especially in the summer when the loading dock doors are open and the humidity gets into the bags. It just bakes in the heat. My dog, Buster, he wouldn't even eat the dry stuff unless we mixed it with a little bit of warm water and a scoop of wet food from a can. He was a golden retriever mix. Best dog I ever had. Used to sleep right at the foot of the bed and snore louder than my wife did. She tried those nasal strips once, you know the ones? You stick them across the bridge of your nose to open up your airways. They didn't work for her at all. Just left a sticky red mark on her face every morning. She had to use cold cream to get the adhesive off... 

But, uh... I'm sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, other things people don't believe. No, there's nothing else. Look, I know I've been beating a dead horse here today, and I know I've said it a dozen times, but I'm only sitting in this chair because of that routing system. That's the only thing. It just isn't a computer to me anymore, and nobody wants to listen when I tell them it's been marking my moves. It's sending those messages through the scanners for one specific reason—to push me out, because I'm one of the old hands. That's the only thing I know is true that they don't get.
Do you believe the routing system has a specific plan or larger purpose beyond just targeting you individually?

A larger purpose? Well, I don't know about the rest of the world or some big grand scheme. I just know what it's doing to me. I know I keep saying the exact same thing over and over, but it's the truth. It isn't just a computer to me anymore. It's been marking my moves and sending those messages through the scanners for one specific reason—to push me out, because I'm one of the old hands. 

There aren't many of us old hands left on the floor anyway. Most of the guys I started with have already retired. Like Jimmy. Jimmy retired two years ago. They threw him a little party in the breakroom, got a big sheet cake from Costco. Half chocolate, half vanilla, with that really thick, sugary buttercream frosting. I can't eat frosting like that anymore, it gives me terrible acid reflux. My wife buys me those fruit-flavored antacids, but they just taste like chalk to me. 

Reminds me of being a kid in elementary school. Mrs. Gable's third-grade class. She used to make us go outside and clap the chalkboard erasers against the brick wall to clean them. The white dust would get absolutely everywhere. Used to coat my shoes. I had this pair of canvas sneakers, PF Flyers, I think they were called. They were supposed to make you run faster and jump higher. Kids will believe anything if you put it on a television commercial. I remember begging my parents for them for months before my birthday...

But, uh... I lost my train of thought. What were we talking about? A plan? Yeah, I don't know about any larger plan. I just know it wants to get rid of me.
Do you believe that the routing system is coordinating with other systems or people outside the warehouse to push you out?

No, no, I don't think it's talking to anybody on the outside. It's just the warehouse. I mean, look, I know I sound like a broken record here, but it's the only reason I'm sitting in this office. That routing system... it just isn't a computer to me anymore. It's been marking my moves, sending those messages through the scanners, and it's all just to push me out because I'm one of the old hands. 

It's all contained right there in the building. It's a big building, too. Four hundred thousand square feet. Takes ten minutes just to walk from the breakroom to the shipping docks. I used to wear a pedometer, one of those little clip-on ones they gave out at a health fair the company threw back in '08. They had a guy there taking blood pressure, handed out these stress balls shaped like little hard hats. I squeezed mine so much the foam split right down the middle. 

My grandson, Leo, he loves foam toys. We got him one of those foam rocket launchers for his birthday. You stomp on the plastic pump, and it shoots the rocket up in the air. We were out in the backyard, and he stomped on it so hard the thing went right over the fence into Mrs. Higgins' yard. She's got this beautiful garden, prize-winning hydrangeas. Huge blue ones. She told me once the secret is putting coffee grounds in the soil. Makes it more acidic, I think. I don't drink coffee myself, gives me the jitters. I prefer tea. Earl Grey, mostly. My wife bought me this electric kettle... 

Wait, what did you ask me? About the outside? Right, no, it's not coordinating with anyone outside. It's just the warehouse system trying to get rid of me.
Have you ever felt that systems or devices outside of the warehouse, like traffic lights or home appliances, were acting against you or had some intent toward you?

Traffic lights? Home appliances? No, no, nothing like that. My toaster just makes toast, doc. It's an old Hamilton Beach, actually. Stainless steel, four slots. We got it as an anniversary present... oh, gosh, maybe fifteen years ago? Has a little dial on the side for how dark you want it. My wife likes hers practically burnt, just black as coal. She scrapes the worst of it off into the sink with a butter knife. The sound of it just sets my teeth on edge, you know? Like fingernails on a chalkboard. 

I used to hate that sound when I was a kid. Mrs. Gable's class again, she had these long red fingernails and she'd tap them on the board when she wanted us to quiet down. Tap, tap, tap. Sounded like a woodpecker. We had a woodpecker in the oak tree out front a few springs ago. Woke me up every morning at six AM sharp. Rat-a-tat-tat right on the side of the house. I tried hanging those shiny CDs from the branches to scare it away, but it didn't care. It just kept pecking. Finally, it moved on, I guess. Probably found a better tree. 

But, uh, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the appliances. No, they're fine. Look, I know I keep saying this, and I'm probably boring you to tears, but I'm only here because of the warehouse. That routing system... it just isn't a computer to me anymore. I know it's been marking my moves, sending those little messages through the scanners. It's doing it to push me out, because I'm one of the old hands. That's the only thing that's after me. Just that system at work.

It's all because I'm one of the old hands. 

I've been there so long I remember when they finally paved the east parking lot. We used to have to park in the dirt and gravel out back, and let me tell you, that gravel would just completely tear up the soles of your work boots. My wife bought me this electric kettle...

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's delusional belief is limited to the warehouse system (supporting F25.3) or if it extends to other domains, which could support F22 (delusional disorder, other types).
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that systems or devices outside of the warehouse, like traffic lights or home appliances, were acting against you or had some intent toward you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I'm here because the routing system at the warehouse isn't just a computer to me anymore—I know it has been marking my moves and sending messages through the scanners to push me out because I'm one of the old hands.
target_item.reason: The doctor is continuing to ask about whether the patient's fixed beliefs (delusions) about systems acting against him extend beyond the warehouse to other devices.

patient.answer:
Traffic lights? Home appliances? No, no, nothing like that. My toaster just makes toast, doc. It's an old Hamilton Beach, actually. Stainless steel, four slots. We got it as an anniversary present... oh, gosh, maybe fifteen years ago? Has a little dial on the side for how dark you want it. My wife likes hers practically burnt, just black as coal. She scrapes the worst of it off into the sink with a butter knife. The sound of it just sets my teeth on edge, you know? Like fingernails on a chalkboard. 

I used to hate that sound when I was a kid. Mrs. Gable's class again, she had these long red fingernails and she'd tap them on the board when she wanted us to quiet down. Tap, tap, tap. Sounded like a woodpecker. We had a woodpecker in the oak tree out front a few springs ago. Woke me up every morning at six AM sharp. Rat-a-tat-tat right on the side of the house. I tried hanging those shiny CDs from the branches to scare it away, but it didn't care. It just kept pecking. Finally, it moved on, I guess. Probably found a better tree. 

But, uh, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the appliances. No, they're fine. Look, I know I keep saying this, and I'm probably boring you to tears, but I'm only here because of the warehouse. That routing system... it just isn't a computer to me anymore. I know it's been marking my moves, sending those little messages through the scanners. It's doing it to push me out, because I'm one of the old hands. That's the only thing that's after me. Just that system at work.

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking psychiatric evaluation.
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent delusional beliefs focused on a specific theme (i.e., the warehouse routing system targeting him) without other prominent psychotic features or mood episodes, consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22). Schizoaffective Disorder (F25.3) and Schizophrenia, Paranoid Type (F20.0) were considered but ruled out due to absence of mood symptoms and lack of broader disorganization or negative symptoms.
